newsitem.title: CHINA: China to establish regulations for BOT.
newsitem.headline: China to establish regulations for BOT.

text.p: China is planning to expand the number of projects using the BOT (build operate transfer) system and the State Planning Commission would submit rules governing the process for approval, the Business News said on Monday.
The State Council, China's cabinet, was expected to authorise the rules before the end of this month, it said.
BOT refers to the practice of allowing foreign investors to build plants and operate them for profit over a specified number of years before the plant's operation is transferred to the host country.
The newspaper said the commission recently added two more BOT projects, the Changsha Electrical Generator Plant and the Chengdu Waterworks.

China signed its first completely foreign-financed BOT deal in November 1996, a $589.9 million agreement with French utility company Electricite de France and GEC-Alsthom ALSF.CN to build a power station in Guangxi province, company officials said earlier.
"Judging from completed BOT deals, this type of investment has a great deal of potential," a commission offical told the newspaper.
"The Planning Commission is working hard to make this type of investment more common in China," he said.
